subject: Trading
title: The Role of Commodity Traders
description: A fast breakdown of The Role of Commodity Traders for builders.

hook.text: Vitol, Glencore, and Trafigura move more oil than most countries produce. They're trillion-dollar middlemen.

buildup.text: Commodity trading houses buy raw materials from producers and sell to consumers—managing logistics, risk, and finance.

discovery.text: They profit from logistics: moving oil from where it's cheap to where it's expensive, arbitraging price gaps.

twist.text: These firms are mostly private and secretive. They control trillions in goods with limited public oversight.

climax.text: Commodity traders are the invisible plumbing of the global economy—connecting supply to demand across every continent.

punchline.text: The richest middlemen you've never heard of.

quiz.question: How do commodity trading houses primarily make money?
options: Arbitraging price differences and managing logistics between producers and consumers
